hunt.justification: The September 2026 Patch Tuesday includes 999 vulnerabilities, with confirmed zero-day exploitation of ALPC and Update Stack mechanisms. Identifying unpatched hosts and verifying they are clean of exploitation is a critical requirement given the high potential for automated ransomware deployment.

meta.name: Windows Zero-Day Privilege Escalation and Ransomware

related.reason: Adversaries frequently use similar privilege escalation patterns across different Windows services like the Print Spooler or Fax Service.

meta.analysis: A vulnerability scanner only reports the missing patch. This hunt pivots to look for the rare SYSTEM-integrity processes and symbolic link artifacts that prove the vulnerability is being actively weaponized in this environment, using a prevalence baseline to filter out legitimate system activity.

coverage.reason: Exploit payloads for zero-days in network services are generally not visible in standard hb_http_activity or hb_network_connection without deep packet inspection.

stages.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
observables: Inbound exploitation attempts against internet-facing Windows services

stages.name: ALPC Buffer Overflow Elevation
observables: Buffer overflow in Advanced Local Procedure Call (ALPC) mechanism
Process integrity escalation to SYSTEM from user-mode processes

stages.name: Update Stack Link Resolution Elevation
observables: Improper link resolution in Windows Update Stack
Creation of symbolic links or junctions in update paths by low-privileged users

stages.name: Ransomware Data Encryption
observables: Bulk file write and rename operations
Encryption of common user files (Office docs, PDFs, images)
System-wide file markers or new extensions

scenario.summary: The September 2026 Patch Tuesday released 999 CVEs, featuring two zero-day elevation of privilege vulnerabilities in the Windows ALPC (CVE-2026-85880) and Update Stack (CVE-2026-81963) exploited in the wild. Attackers use these flaws to escalate to SYSTEM privileges on Windows systems, often as a precursor to ransomware deployment and bulk file encryption.

meta.rationale: Prioritize domain controllers and internet-facing application servers. Use device_uid from the first query to identify the specific assets before widening the search to the entire workstation fleet.
meta.hypothesis: Adversaries are exploiting unpatched Windows ALPC or Update Stack vulnerabilities to escalate to SYSTEM integrity and deploy ransomware, leaving traces of rare process elevations and specific link-resolution artifacts.

cve_ids.description: Vulnerability identifiers for the September zero-days.

scope_hosts.description: Limit behavioral checks to these hostnames; leave empty to hunt across the entire estate.

blind_spots.risk: The hunt only sees the aftermath of elevation; a failed exploit attempt or one that stays in-kernel would be missed.
blind_spots.question: whether the ALPC buffer overflow occurred without causing a process launch
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy EDR policies with kernel-level exploit protection and enable advanced auditing for ALPC events.

blind_spots.risk: Initial exploitation attempts against Windows web services are invisible to endpoint logs without traffic inspection.
blind_spots.question: whether specific exploit strings were delivered via HTTPS to internet-facing services
blind_spots.remediation: Enable SSL/TLS inspection for inbound traffic to critical servers and monitored web endpoints.

hunt.name: Windows Zero-Day Privilege Escalation and Ransomware
hunt.description: This hunt targets the zero-day exploits published in September 2026 (CVE-2026-85880 and CVE-2026-81963). The ALPC buffer overflow and Update Stack link resolution flaws allow low-privileged attackers to gain SYSTEM access. Once elevated, the adversary is expected to deploy ransomware. The hunt identifies vulnerable assets, baselines rare SYSTEM-integrity processes, and triages specific file system behaviors such as suspicious symbolic link creation in update directories and high-volume file encryption markers.

config.content: SELECT device_uid, cve_uid, severity, status FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE instr(',' || '{{cve_ids}}' || ',', ',' || cve_uid || ',') > 0 AND status != 'suppressed' AND status != 'fixed'
config.description: The hunt identifies unpatched Windows endpoints missing fixes for the ALPC and Update Stack zero-days to establish the scope of exposed assets.
config.expected_signal: A list of device_uids that are unpatched. Silence means the estate is fully patched against these specific CVEs.

primitive_config.label: Identify vulnerable Windows endpoints
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_uid, cve_uid, severity, status FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE instr(',' || '{{cve_ids}}' || ',', ',' || cve_uid || ',') > 0 AND status != 'suppressed' AND status != 'fixed'
primitive_config.expected: A list of device_uids that are unpatched. Silence means the estate is fully patched against these specific CVEs.

config.content: SELECT process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(integrity_level) = 'system' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_name HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: This hunt pivots to look for the rare SYSTEM-integrity processes and symbolic link artifacts that prove the vulnerability is being actively weaponized.
config.expected_signal: A small set of processes running with System privileges on only 1-3 hosts. Legitimate system utilities will show high host counts.

primitive_config.label: Baseline rare SYSTEM-integrity processes
primitive_config.content: SELECT process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE LOWER(integrity_level) = 'system' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_name HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
primitive_config.expected: A small set of processes running with System privileges on only 1-3 hosts. Legitimate system utilities will show high host counts.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE file_type = 'symlink' AND LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\windows\softwaredistribution%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: The hunt detects the specific 'improper link resolution' behavior where an adversary creates symbolic links in Windows Update paths to gain SYSTEM privileges.
config.expected_signal: Any symbolic links created within the Windows Update paths (SoftwareDistribution) by non-system processes.

primitive_config.label: Update stack symbolic link creation
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, file_path, process_name, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_file_activity WHERE file_type = 'symlink' AND LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\windows\softwaredistribution%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Any symbolic links created within the Windows Update paths (SoftwareDistribution) by non-system processes.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, COUNT(*) AS write_count, MAX(time) AS last_write FROM hb_file_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.crypt%' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.locked%' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE 'read_me%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname HAVING write_count > 5
config.description: The hunt identifies high-volume file encryption and rename markers that indicate a successful ransomware impact following the privilege escalation.
config.expected_signal: Hosts showing multiple file writes with known ransomware extensions or note filenames.

primitive_config.label: High-volume file encryption activity
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, COUNT(*) AS write_count, MAX(time) AS last_write FROM hb_file_activity WHERE ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND (LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.crypt%' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE '%.locked%' OR LOWER(file_name) LIKE 'read_me%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname HAVING write_count > 5
primitive_config.expected: Hosts showing multiple file writes with known ransomware extensions or note filenames.

config.objective: Analyze the combination of unpatched status, rare system processes, and suspicious file activity to determine if an adversary has compromised any exposed host.
config.description: Analyze the combination of unpatched status, rare system processes, and suspicious file activity to determine if an adversary has compromised a host.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign, citing specific process launches or file paths.

config.question: the agent-triage verdict indicates active exploitation or ransomware activity on any exposed host
config.condition: the agent-triage verdict indicates active exploitation or ransomware activity on any exposed host
config.description: Route the hunt to remediation tasks if active exploitation is found, or general patching if only exposure is confirmed.
The analyst ensures the vulnerable hosts are patched and confirms no further compromise exists.
config.instructions: For hosts identified as vulnerable or compromised: 1. Deploy the September 2026 security updates for Windows ALPC and Update Stack. 2. Verify patch installation via hb_vulnerability_finding. 3. If the agent identified malicious behavior, escalate to the Incident Response team for host forensic imaging.
